newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani bourse appeals for higher dividends.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani bourse appeals for higher dividends.

text.p: Arif Habib, president of the Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE), on Sunday appealed to listed firms to declare higher cash dividends to help a revival of investors' confidence.
"We have called upon the managements of a number of listed companies to declare enhanced cash dividend to help the institutional and individual investors," Habib told the KSE's board meeting.
The government had announced measures for the stock exchanges which would help in the restoration of investors confidence in the equity market, Habib said.
"The year 1997 has started with KSE 100 index at a near record low for the last three years," Habib said.

"It is due to the alarming weakness of the national economy and of the local financial institutions along with uncertainties associated with general elections which are scheduled for February 3 this year," he said.

"Investors' confidence in the equity investment is at a very low ebb but large number of choices are available to invest in shares with very low P/Es (price earnings) and quoting much below their book value," Habib said.
